5-1.question: Which statements about 坎坎糊 (four concealed Pungs) are correct?
options: It is a limit hand worth 10 Faan
A Kong is allowed among the four sets
A single-tile wait (單吊) may win on a discard
A pair wait (對碰) must be won by self-draw
5-1.explanation: 坎坎糊 is a 10-Faan limit hand with four concealed Pungs and no Kongs; a single wait may take a discard but a pair wait must be self-drawn.

5-1.question: Match each hand shape to what it is called.

pairs.left: Four Pongs or Kongs plus a pair

5-1.explanation: All Pongs is 對對糊, its all-Chow opposite is 平糊, four Kongs is 十八羅漢, and one suit with honors is 混一色.

5-1.question: Going for All Pongs, your 13 tiles are {{m3}}{{m3}}{{m3}} {{p7}}{{p7}}{{p7}} {{s1}}{{s1}}{{s1}} {{red}}{{red}}{{red}} {{east}}. Which tile completes the hand?
5-1.explanation: {{east}} becomes the pair for the eyes; the other four sets are already triplets.

5-1.question: All Pongs is 3 Faan and Mixed One Suit is 3 Faan. An All Pongs hand built from one suit plus honors scores how many Faan in total?
5-1.explanation: The two patterns stack, so 3 + 3 = 6 Faan, safely under the 10-Faan cap.

5-1.question: A hand is four Pongs plus a pair. Can it also be scored as 平糊 (All Chows)?
options: Yes, if the hand is concealed
Yes, if it is won by self-draw
No — 平糊 needs four Chows and no triplets
No — 平糊 needs honor tiles
5-1.explanation: 平糊 requires four Chows with no Pong or Kong, so it can never combine with 對對糊.

5-2.question: Match each part of Thirteen Orphans (十三么) to its count.

pairs.left: Terminal types in the set (1s and 9s)
Types duplicated to make the pair

5-2.explanation: Six terminals (1 and 9 of each suit) and seven honors make the 13 types, one of which is duplicated.

5-2.question: Which statements about Thirteen Orphans (十三么) are correct?
options: It needs one of each of the 13 terminal and honor types
One of those types is duplicated to form the pair
It has no melds at all — no Chows, Pongs or Kongs
It may include one Chow as long as the hand stays concealed
5-2.explanation: 十三么 is 13 single tiles plus one duplicate, so it contains no Chows, Pongs or Kongs.

5-2.question: Which of these tiles is NOT used in Thirteen Orphans (十三么)?
5-2.explanation: Only 1s, 9s and honor tiles qualify, so the middle tile {{m5}} never appears.

5-2.question: How many tiles does a completed Thirteen Orphans (十三么) hand contain?
5-2.explanation: Thirteen different types plus the duplicated tile make 14 tiles.

5-2.question: Your opponent declares a concealed Kong (暗槓). Which hand is allowed to rob it?
options: Any hand worth at least 3 Faan
5-2.explanation: 搶槓 normally only robs an added Kong, but 十三么 is the one hand that may rob a concealed Kong.

5-3.question: Your hand is a Full Flush (清一色) in Bamboo. Which of these tiles would break it?
5-3.explanation: 清一色 uses exactly one suit with no honors, so any Character tile breaks the flush.

5-3.question: Arrange these Character tiles into a Chow — Full Flush restricts the suit, not the meld shape.
5-3.explanation: A Chow is three consecutive tiles of one suit, so 2-3-4 of Characters is correct.

5-3.question: Which of these hands are Full Flush (清一色)?
5-3.explanation: The first two are single-suit hands, while the third carries a Dragon triplet and the fourth is all honors (字一色).

5-3.question: Full Flush is 7 Faan and All Pongs is 3 Faan. A one-suit All Pongs hand with no honors scores how many Faan?
5-3.explanation: 7 + 3 = 10 Faan, which lands exactly on the 10-Faan cap.

5-3.question: Does Full Flush (清一色) require a particular meld type?
options: Yes, it must be all Chows
Yes, it must be all Pongs
No — it only restricts the suit
No — honor tiles are also allowed
5-3.explanation: 清一色 is defined by suit alone, so Chows and Pongs can be mixed freely.

5-4.question: Which of these tiles can appear in 清么九 (All Terminals)?
5-4.explanation: 清么九 uses only the 1s and 9s of the three suits — no middle tiles and no honors.

5-4.question: Match each limit hand to the tiles it allows.
5-4.explanation: These four hands differ exactly in which tile groups are permitted.

5-4.question: How many different tile types can appear in 清么九 (All Terminals)?
5-4.explanation: Each suit contributes a 1 and a 9, so only six types qualify.

5-4.question: Which of these tiles could NOT appear in 字一色 (All Honors)?
5-4.explanation: 字一色 is made only of Wind and Dragon tiles, so any suited tile is impossible.

5-4.question: {{m1}}{{m1}}{{m1}} {{m9}}{{m9}}{{m9}} {{p1}}{{p1}}{{p1}} {{s9}}{{s9}}{{s9}} {{p9}}{{p9}} — which hand is this?
5-4.explanation: Every tile is a 1 or a 9 with no honors, which is exactly 清么九 — a 10-Faan limit hand.

5-5.question: Match each special hand to what it requires.

pairs.right: One of each of the 13 terminal and honor types
Four triplets or Kongs plus a pair
A single suit with no honors

5-5.explanation: Each name maps to one defining condition: all 13 singles, all triplets, one suit, or honors only.

5-5.question: Which of these are limit hands counted as 10 Faan?
5-5.explanation: 清一色 is 7 Faan and 對對糊 is 3; the other three are 例牌 scored at 10.

5-5.question: A limit hand is won by self-draw. How much does each of the three opponents pay?
5-5.explanation: At 10 Faan a self-draw costs each opponent 64, for 192 collected in total.

5-5.question: Arrange these tiles into a Chow — the meld All Pongs forbids but Full Flush allows.
5-5.explanation: A Chow is three consecutive tiles of one suit, so 4-5-6 of Bamboo is correct.

5-5.question: A hand is four Pongs plus a pair, all in one suit with no honors. How many Faan does it score?
5-5.explanation: 清一色 (7) + 對對糊 (3) = 10 Faan, which is the cap.
